newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Organon settles gene amplification dispute.
newsitem.headline: Organon settles gene amplification dispute.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Thursday its pharmaceutical unit Organon Teknika had settled a patent dispute with Stanford University and Gen-Probe Incorporated over gene-amplification technology.

"Stanford agreed to convert Gen-Probe's exclusive licence to its patent rights in the field to a co-exclusive licence to enable both Gen-Probe and Teknika to practice under those patents," Akzo said in a statement.

"Additionally, Teknika and Gen-Probe signed a mutual non-assertion agreement that permits each to practice and license its respective versions of transcription-based amplification without being concerned about possible infringement of the other party's patents."
The technology is the foundation of a new generation of tests for diagnosing infectious diseases, cancer and genetic disorders, Akzo said.

"Because it can produce billions of copies of cell components (nucleic acids) characteristic of particular disease states, tests that are much more accurate and sensitive than previous ones can be developed."
Organon could now rapidly expand its NucliSens product line, which uses the technique, the company said. The line currently consists of testing kits for the HIV virus.
